PullRequest.Title: Add opt-in merging of document highlight providers
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #48821.

## Summary

This PR allows displaying all document highlights from all DocumentHighlightProviders. This PR adds a setting `editor.occurrencesHighlightFromAllProviders` which defaults to `false`. It uses the built-in word-matching fallback only when no other provider matches.

## Manual verification

- [x] With `editor.occurrencesHighlightFromAllProviders` unset or `false`, verify document highlights keep the existing first-answer behavior.
- [x] Enable the setting and verify highlights from multiple matching single-document providers appear together.
- [x] Verify identical ranges are shown once and use the higher-priority provider's highlight kind, regardless of completion order.
- [x] Verify the built-in word-matching fallback is used only when no registered provider returns a result.
- [x] Toggle the setting while an editor is open and verify highlighting updates without reopening it.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed command call, Promise.all fan-out, per-provider RPC bridge, tsserver request, absence of cancellation, and before/after short-circuit behavior are all directly traced. Only prevalence is uncertain because the option is opt-in and requires an API-command caller plus multiple matching providers; that limits severity, not mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: main-thread-to-extension-host IPC calls and downstream language-provider/language-server requests
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For each vscode.executeDocumentHighlights invocation, work grows from providers queried only until the first non-null answer (normally one) to all P matching non-textual providers concurrently; repeated command calls multiply this by the call frequency.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased command latency to the slowest provider plus avoidable IPC, extension-host CPU, and language-server load.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The command called getOccurrencesAtPosition without merge mode, whose first(...) loop stopped as soon as the highest-priority provider returned a non-null result.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The command now reads editor.occurrencesHighlightFromAllProviders and passes it into getOccurrencesAtPosition; when enabled, that helper uses Promise.all over every matching provider.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 230 newly passes mergeProviders into the API command's getOccurrencesAtPosition call; this is the exact switch from the pre-diff first-success path to the added all-provider Promise.all path.
Findings.Title: Keep the editor merge setting out of the API command
Findings.Impact: When a user enables the editor-only merge option and an extension invokes vscode.executeDocumentHighlights, each invocation now starts all matching providers and waits for the slowest. With overlapping language extensions, command-driven navigation or analysis becomes slower and can burst multiple extension-host/language-server requests even though the API command previously needed only the first successful answer.
Findings.Evidence: The added command argument at line 230 reaches the new Promise.all provider loop at lines 48-55. Extension providers cross one $provideDocumentHighlights RPC per registration in mainThreadLanguageFeatures.ts:327-330, and the built-in TypeScript provider then issues a documentHighlights request to tsserver in extensions/typescript-language-features/src/languageFeatures/documentHighlight.ts:63. The command supplies CancellationToken.None, so this non-UI API path has no cancellation and cannot complete until every provider settles.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep _executeDocumentHighlights on the existing first-answer behavior (pass false) and apply the setting only in WordHighlighter; if API callers need merged results, expose that as an explicit cancellable API choice rather than inheriting a global editor option.

Scenarios.Scenario: Automatic single-document occurrence highlighting with the new option disabled (default)
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After an explicit cursor move is coalesced by the 50 ms Delayer, the highest-priority provider must return a non-null result before decorations can render; lower-priority providers are queried only when earlier providers decline.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke an extension-host document highlight provider via $provideDocumentHighlights.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one call per distinct highlighted word when the first matching provider succeeds; at most providers through the first non-null answer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same sequential first-answer boundary behavior existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The selected provider response is on the decoration-rendering critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: A provider such as TypeScript sends documentHighlights to its language server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One tsserver request when TypeScript is the selected provider for a highlight request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The selected provider already performed this request before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The language-server response must return before highlights render.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct explicit cursor positions/words after 50 ms coalescing, and the number of providers that decline before the first successful provider.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One provider is awaited at a time through first(...); cursor movement cancels the current request and the Delayer coalesces movements within 50 ms.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Registry selector scores are reused for an unchanged model candidate, but provider results are not cached; moving within existing decorations avoids a new request.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; the unchanged first(...) path and trigger/cancellation flow were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency varies by extension and language server, but this default scenario is behaviorally unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the default setting preserves the prior provider cardinality and critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Automatic single-document occurrence highlighting with occurrencesHighlightFromAllProviders enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After cursor-event coalescing, all matching non-textual providers are started and Promise.all must settle before merged ranges are deduplicated and decorations render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke each matching extension-host document highlight provider through a separate $provideDocumentHighlights call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: P calls per distinct highlighted word, where P is the effective number of matching non-textual providers after selector/exclusive filtering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Providers were queried sequentially only through the first non-null answer, normally one call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Promise.all places the slowest provider response on the rendering critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Matching language-backed providers can issue one document-highlight request to their language server, as TypeScript does with tsserver.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one downstream request per matching language-backed provider per distinct highlighted word.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only providers reached before the first successful result issued downstream requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All provider requests must settle before merged decorations render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Flatten P result arrays, construct a range key for every returned highlight, and deduplicate into one decoration list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: O(H) work and temporary entries, where H is the total highlights returned by all P providers before deduplication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No cross-provider flattening or deduplication occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously after all providers settle and before decoration rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number P of matching providers and total returned highlights H, repeated for distinct cursor words after 50 ms event coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Promise.all starts all P providers concurrently. A subsequent cursor request cancels the current token; compliant providers stop, while the outer cancelable promise rejects immediately.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No provider-result cache or request coalescing beyond the cursor Delayer and reuse while the cursor remains within existing decoration ranges.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; fan-out, cancellation, merge allocation, and decoration critical path are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: P is commonly small and the option is explicitly opt-in; provider duration and cancellation compliance vary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for the editor flow because querying and merging all providers is the explicit opt-in feature semantics; concurrency minimizes aggregate latency and cancellation is propagated.

Scenarios.Scenario: Extension invokes vscode.executeDocumentHighlights while the editor merge option is enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The API command now reads the editor option, starts all matching providers, and waits for Promise.all and merge processing before returning to the calling extension.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Issue one $provideDocumentHighlights main-thread-to-extension-host call for each matching provider registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: P calls per API invocation rather than providers only through the first non-null answer, normally one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The command used the first-answer path and stopped after the first non-null provider result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The API command cannot return until the slowest of all P providers settles.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Language-backed providers may each dispatch a document-highlight request, including TypeScript's tsserver request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one downstream language-server request for each matching language-backed provider per command invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only a provider reached before the first successful result could issue this work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All such requests are included in Promise.all and can delay command completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number P of overlapping matching provider registrations multiplied by the frequency with which an extension invokes the API command.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All P providers start concurrently. The command passes CancellationToken.None, so callers have no cancellation or backpressure for this wave.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No result cache, negative cache, or in-flight coalescing; every command invocation repeats the provider and downstream work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high; the changed argument, Promise.all path, RPC registration, tsserver request, and non-cancellable token are all directly evidenced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The option is opt-in and third-party command-call frequency is not visible in-repository, limiting severity; overlapping providers are explicitly supported and the boundary multiplication is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out: an editor presentation preference unnecessarily changes an independent API command from first-success work to all-provider IPC and slowest-provider latency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all eight changed files. Traced editor cursor highlighting, configuration toggling, provider merging/deduplication, extension-host RPC, the TypeScript language-server boundary, cancellation, caching, effective concurrency, and the public API-command path. Submitted one medium-confidence-independent, high-mechanism-confidence finding for avoidable API-command fan-out; the opt-in editor merge cost itself matches the requested feature semantics.
